review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Suppress the click callback for disabled links**

Whenever a disabled link is activated without a pointer—for example, it was focused before `disabled` changed, assistive technology activates it, or code calls `.click()`—this wrapper prevents the href's default navigation but immediately invokes the consumer's `onClick`. A handler that routes or performs an action therefore still activates a control that is advertised as disabled (unlike a native disabled `<button>`); do not call the supplied handler in this branch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope pointer-event disabling to anchor-backed buttons**

Whenever an ordinary native button is disabled inside another clickable surface (for example, an action inside a clickable card), this rule also assigns `pointer-events: none` because `_disabled` is not anchor-specific. Hit testing then skips the button and targets the clickable ancestor or content underneath, so clicking the visibly disabled control can trigger a different action; apply this rule only to anchor-backed disabled buttons rather than every disabled `Button`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
